thread:
olivia: Heads-up — onboarding fenrir-7b-hf. conversion produced a config.json that looks wrong and evals show a consistent quality drop after 4-bit quant. quick paste of converted fields:

```
{
  "rope_scaling": "linear",
  "sliding_window": false,
  "num_key_value_heads": 32,
  "max_position_embeddings": 2048
}
```

olivia: I ran some shape checks against the hf checkpoint and the attn kv shapes imply 16 KV heads and 4096 max pos. so the converter bumped heads and truncated maxpos.

ben: which converter flags? did you use --preserve-config or let the tool normalize?

olivia: i used `hf-to-redwood convert --auto` (latest tool). didn't pass explicit overrides.

carlos: sounds like two separate mismatches: rope scaling semantics + kv head parity. our runtime assumes num_key_value_heads matches weight grouping — if mismatched attention splits get misaligned and quant amplifies the error.

olivia: small repro snippet i ran to inspect weights:

```
python - <<'PY'
import torch
w = torch.load('pytorch_model.bin', map_location='cpu')
for k in ('model.attn.q_proj.weight','model.attn.k_proj.weight','model.attn.v_proj.weight'):
    if k in w:
        print(k, w[k].shape)
PY
```

olivia: output showed q/k/v shapes consistent with 16 heads (hidden_per_head ~ 64) and token embeddings for 4096 positions.


diay: (typo: Diya) our bench shows ~+12% perplexity on common-sense suite after 4-bit quant when converter left sliding_window off. chat templates rely on sliding_window to preserve chat markers, otherwise early tokens get truncated in prefix cache during streaming -> quality regression.

ben: two immediate remediation steps: 1) set num_key_value_heads to actual heads (16) in the converted config; 2) set max_position_embeddings to the model's 4096. also enable sliding_window=true for chat-style configs.

carlos: i'll run a quick compare job on dedicated infra: baseline float32 run vs int4 quant with the patched config, and push eval metrics to the bench dashboard. grabbing the model now.

olivia: i also noticed rope_scaling originally in HF was an object: `{
  "type": "dynamic",
  "factor": 0.5
}` but converter flattened to string `linear`. that changes interpolation for long-context attention. quant + wrong rope scaling => attention drift at >1024 tokens.

ben: ah — converter should map object -> runtime rope config struct. filed a tiny issue: https://git.redwood/infra/hf-converter/issues/412 (short summary).

diya: for now, can we add a quick sanity-check script to the converter that validates: num_key_value_heads * head_dim == qkv_dim and max_position_embeddings >= tokenizer.model_max_length? saves another triage.

carlos: agreed. i'll add the head/pos check and a warning + auto-fix flag. will ping when PR is up.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: eng-ml/converter#fix-head-pos-check -> staging (job 6124).

olivia: thanks — once PR lands i'll re-run quant eval and post results. current plan: patch config -> reconvert weights -> run int4 eval against bench.

ben: solid — flag me if you see any remaining tokenization drift; also share a small failing prompt that reproduces the hallucination/regression so QA can add a regression test.

olivia: will drop an example prompt + before/after outputs after CARLOS's run. :thumbsup:
